water-heating-curve.alt: Heating curve of water, temperature against energy added (not to scale): ice warms to 0 °C, a flat part while ice melts (q = n·ΔHfus), liquid warms to 100 °C (q = m·c·ΔT), a much longer flat part while water boils (q = n·ΔHvap), then steam warms. On the flat parts the temperature is constant and the energy overcomes attractions between molecules.
